title: Introduce sampled provenance tokens for post-hoc tail reconstruction
creator: Maya Chen
description:
Background: Tail investigations require retaining or replaying full spans which increases hotpath allocations and retention costs. Goal: provide a compact, low-cost artifact produced in the hotpath that enables deterministic post-hoc reconstruction of a trace segment (the tail window) without keeping full span payloads on the hotpath.

Design summary: emit a 'sampled provenance token' (SPT) per request when sampling heuristics indicate potential tail relevance. SPT is a fixed-size, ~48-96 byte, cryptographically signed compact blob containing: route hash, per-request minimal timing watermark, up-to-N KV-cache digests, and a hashed pointer (seg-id) that can be resolved by a background assembler service. The hotpath only allocates the token (byte slice) and performs one non-blocking enqueue to a bounded token queue; heavy operations (resolution, full-span aggregation) are done off-hotpath.

Adaptive behavior: sampling rate for SPTs is driven by a per-route feedback loop (latency/error budget) and a tail-triggered retention policy: when tail signals appear from metrics pipeline, the assembler will request retroactive retention for recent token seg-ids to rebuild context.

Success metrics: 1) reduce hotpath allocation bytes for trace-bearing requests by >= 40% vs baseline, 2) maintain root-cause resolution rate within 90% of full-span retention for sampled incidents, 3) end-to-end tail reconstruction latency < 60s after trigger.

Trade-offs and risks: tokens still add network/queue pressure; signature key management required for replay safety; assembler introduces eventual consistency in debugability. We avoid storing PII by hashing any user-provided keys and truncating fields.

Rollout plan: 1) feature-flag SPT emission in canary region for non-prod routes; 2) enable per-route low-rate sampling (0.1%) + tail-detection hooks in metrics; 3) expand sampling rules and tuning; 4) expose dashboard and refinement controls in Console.

Artifacts: design doc https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OBS/SPT-design, draft PR https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/pull/5142, metrics dashboard (internal) https://dashboards.redwood.ai/d/trace-spt/overview
comments: 2026-02-16 - Maya Chen: Initial spike shows token allocation overhead ~120B vs full-span ~2.4KB for sampled path. Background assembler prototype can resolve 95% of provenance keys with a 30s window.
2026-02-22 - Diego Alvarez: Implemented bounded token queue and backpressure metrics. Observed queue saturation during bursty traffic; added leaky-drop policy by priority tier.

2026-02-28 - Priya Nair (PM): Reviewed rollout and asked for explicit dashboard widgets: per-route SPT emission rate, queue drop rate, and reconstruction success rate. Added to release acceptance criteria.
2026-03-04 - Security review (initial): Recommended HMAC-based signature with rotated keys and KMS integration. Added KMS rotation task to dependencies.
2026-03-08 - Review feedback from Eng Lead: Move the token assembly to an arena allocator path to avoid many small GC objects in Go. Diego updated implementation PR.
2026-03-10 - Diego Alvarez: Canary enabled on staging; observed 0.6% additional CPU on ingress proxies at 1% SPT rate. Tuned sample rate down for top-traffic routes and added per-route budget checks.
Next steps: complete KMS integration, extend assembler to support cross-tenant resolution, add Console controls for per-route SPT budgets, finalize release notes.
